claim: A frame in which the page chrome and the map disagree about the theme shows a product that fails to repaint its map.
why: It is a broken capture, not a defect of either candidate. Measured: selecting Dark from the theme menu sets the dark ramp on the MapLibre canvas within one second, and frames at +1s and +5s are both fully dark, chrome and map together. The frames that showed a mismatch were shot immediately after a scripted attribute change, before the style document had reloaded.
cost: sank atlas-map-overlay once and wasted parts of rounds 2, 3 and 5

claim: `ReferenceError: document is not defined` in the console is an application error and fails the item.
why: Its stack frame is /@vite/client, the dev server's own HMR message handler. It cannot occur in a build and the Playwright gate never sees it. See the `vite-console-noise` fact.
cost: failed two finished items, atlas-country-actions and atlas-country-card, in round 9

claim: src/lib/map/__tests__/countries.test.ts is too slow and needs its implementation changed.
why: It passes 74/74 when run alone. The 5000ms timeout only appears under the concurrent load a fanned-out round puts on this machine.

claim: The `register` route has a hydration timeout.
why: Seen once in round 2 and never reproduced, on a machine that was carrying sixteen dev servers at the time. A single non-reproducing timeout is a flake.

claim: COL-01, ACC-05, TRP-11 and MNY-07 are the four rows the most other rows depend on.
why: Measured on the edge set and refuted. By transitive in-degree the top five are COL-01 20, ACC-05 16, ADM-02 10, TRP-11 8, MNY-01 8; by direct in-degree DOC-01 leads with 6. Only COL-01 and ACC-05 lead on both readings. MNY-07 and TRP-11 belong early for reasons the graph does not express, which is a different argument and must be made as one.
cost: one blocking and one minor finding, and a wave-table acceptance criterion that could not be satisfied — two rounds

claim: The Playwright chromium visual project is red on main with ~44 failures, so the repo has a pre-existing red floor this run must carry or fix.
why: Every one of those failures was photographed against port 3005, a dev server belonging to a sibling git worktree. Measured on a server started from this checkout: 132 passed, 5 skipped, 0 unexpected, with round 1's changes already in the tree. There is no red floor. See the port-identity-is-the-worktree fact.
cost: the whole of round 1's mechanical verdict, plus an orchestrator investigation that first reached the same wrong conclusion

claim: A console `Failed to load resource: 504 (Outdated Optimize Dep)` from /node_modules/.vite/deps/ is an application error and fails the item.
why: It is Vite's dependency optimiser re-bundling while the page is open — the same class as the vite-console-noise fact. The origin is the dev server's own deps namespace, the gate runs no dev client, and it cannot occur in a build. It failed language-picker in round 4.

claim: Blocking findings the critic writes about candidate A are defects of the item under judgement.
why: A and B are randomised and the critic is blind. In round 4 every 'A's ...' finding on locale-negotiation-shell described the REFERENCE: reading the frames showed B carries our seeded user and our trip 'Japan · Honshu' while A carries 'Japana' and 'Demo User', and abWinner was 'ours'. Check which side won before carrying a critic finding as a defect.
cost: nine phantom blocking findings on an accepted item
